transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I’m here because... everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just normal paperwork and missed payments. They treat it like it's just some standard administrative thing. But I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

It's so obvious. Like at work—I supervise a retail store, and the other day, my cashier, Brenda, she was just standing by the registers texting. I’ve told her a hundred times she can’t be on her phone when the checkout line is backing up into the shoe department. It’s so hard to find reliable people right now, you know? And corporate just keeps sending us these mismatched inventory boxes. It takes me hours to sort through the back room because the barcodes don't even match the shipping manifest. 

But anyway, no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. They are all coordinating this to get me out of my home, and nobody will just admit it.
Do you think people are acting against you personally, or is it just about taking your house?

I don't... I mean, I'm not really sure if it's me specifically or just the property. It's a nice house, you know? It has this beautiful wrap-around porch that I spent all of last summer repainting. Paint is just unbelievably expensive now, too. I went to the hardware store and a single gallon of basic exterior trim paint was like forty-five dollars. And the kid mixing it didn't even hammer the lid down right, so when I put it in the back of my car, it tipped over on the way home. It got all over my floor mats. I tried scrubbing it out with this heavy-duty carpet foam we sell at my store, but honestly, half the cleaning supplies corporate sends us seem watered down lately. Customers complain about it constantly. Brenda had to process three returns just yesterday for this store-brand window spray that leaves streaks everywhere. I keep telling the district manager we need better quality control on our endcaps, but he just ignores my emails... wait, what were you asking me?
How long have you thought that the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job are working together against you?

Well, it’s been about a year and nine months now. That's when the foreclosure notices first started showing up and the bank started calling all the time, just completely taking over our home life. My phone would ring right in the middle of dinner. And speaking of dinner, my husband tried making this new casserole recipe last night that he found on Facebook. He used that really cheap store-brand cheese, the kind that doesn't even melt right? I keep telling him if he’s going to cook, he needs to buy the name brand dairy products. The generic stuff we sell at my store is exactly the same way—it just clumps up and gets oily. We had a lady come in last week demanding a refund on three bags of shredded cheddar because she said it ruined her daughter's birthday party nachos. Brenda tried to explain the return policy on perishable items, but the woman just started screaming. I had to step in, of course, because Brenda just freezes up when people raise their voice. I honestly don't know how she expects to get promoted to assistant manager if she can't even handle a simple customer dispute. I told the district manager... um, wait, I'm sorry, I forgot what we were talking about again. Did I answer your question?
Do you feel like you're having trouble staying on topic when we talk?

I mean... I don't really think so? I'm just trying to give you the full picture, you know? It's important to understand all the pieces. Like, if I don't explain how stressful things are at work, you won't understand why I'm so exhausted all the time. Speaking of exhausted, my husband has been snoring so loudly lately. I don't know if it's his allergies or what, but it's like sleeping next to a chainsaw. I told him he needs to go to the doctor and get one of those CPAP machines. My uncle had one of those, and he said it changed his life. He used to fall asleep right in the middle of family dinners. Just... face first into the mashed potatoes. We had to stop serving gravy because we were afraid he'd drown in it. My aunt was always so embarrassed, but what can you do? It's a medical condition. Just like my cashier Brenda—she says she has a medical condition that makes her need to check her phone every five minutes. I asked her for a doctor's note, and she just rolled her eyes at me. Kids these days, right? They have no respect for authority. I don't know how corporate expects me to run a store when they won't let me write anyone up for... wait, what did you ask me? Am I having trouble with what?
Do you think there's a single person or group directing all of these actions against you, or are they all just working together on their own?

I don't really know if there's one person at the top pulling the strings, or if they just... found each other. It's hard to tell who's really in charge anymore. Kind of like at the store. Our district manager is supposed to be the one directing things, but honestly, I think the vendors have more power than he does. The guy who delivers our soda products? He just does whatever he wants. Last Tuesday, he stacked four pallets of diet cola right in front of the emergency exit. I told him it was a fire hazard, and he just laughed and said he had five more stops to make. I had to get Brenda to help me move them, which of course took forever because she kept stopping to text her boyfriend. They’ve been fighting lately because he wants to buy a motorcycle, and she thinks it’s too dangerous. I agree with her, honestly. My cousin bought a motorcycle back in 2018, and within a week, he laid it down on some wet leaves and broke his collarbone. He had to wear this awful brace for months, and he couldn't even put his own shirt on. His wife had to help him dress every morning, and she was already stressed out because they were trying to remodel their kitchen. Kitchen remodels are just a nightmare. The dust gets everywhere. We had a contractor come look at our kitchen last year before all this bank stuff started, and he quoted us twenty thousand dollars just for cabinets. Can you believe that? Twenty thousand! I told him... wait. What were we talking about? The bank? Who's in charge of what?
Can you explain to me again how you think the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job are all working together against you?

Well, everybody just keeps acting like this whole foreclosure thing is just about paperwork, right? Like it's just missed payments and late fees. But I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And I don't care how many papers they shove in my face, it doesn't change what I've been seeing for almost two years now. It's like they think I'm stupid. Speaking of stupid, my husband bought this new weed whacker last weekend. He went to that big hardware store on the edge of town instead of the one down the street, because he had a coupon. But he didn't read the fine print on the coupon, and it expired in 2022. So he paid full price anyway, and then he couldn't even figure out how to load the string into the thing. He spent three hours in the garage swearing at it. I told him he should just watch a YouTube video on how to do it. That's what I do when the self-checkout machines at the store break down and IT puts me on hold for an hour. You can learn how to fix anything on YouTube. My nephew learned how to rebuild a whole car engine just by watching videos. He bought this old Honda Civic that was completely rusted out, and he spent his entire summer in the driveway taking it apart. His mom was so mad because he got oil stains all over the concrete. Getting oil stains out of concrete is basically impossible. You can try that heavy-duty degreaser, but it just lightens it a little bit. We sell this industrial cleaner at my store, but Brenda keeps putting it in the wrong aisle. I swear, I have told her a hundred times that chemicals go in aisle four, not with the pet supplies. Imagine if someone accidentally bought bleach thinking it was dog shampoo? That would be a disaster. The liability alone... um... wait, what was I saying? Oh right, the bank and the foreclosure. Did that answer what you were asking?
Do you think there's a clear plan or pattern to how these people are working together against you?

I don't really know if there's a specific pattern to it, honestly. I just know they're all in on it together. It's like they're just waiting for me to slip up, you know? Just waiting for one little mistake so they can take everything. Speaking of mistakes, my sister made the biggest mistake last Thanksgiving. She decided she was going to deep-fry the turkey. We all told her it was a bad idea, especially since she wanted to do it on her wooden deck. I mean, who deep-fries a turkey on a wooden deck? It's just asking for a fire. Anyway, she didn't thaw the turkey all the way, and when she dropped it in the oil, it just exploded. Grease went everywhere. Thank god nobody got burned, but the deck was completely ruined. She had to hire a guy to come power-wash and reseal the whole thing, and it cost her like eight hundred dollars. Eight hundred dollars! You could buy a whole new dining room set for that. I was looking at dining sets online the other day because our chairs are getting so wobbly. My husband tried to fix them with wood glue, but he didn't clamp them right, so now they're wobbly and they have dried glue dripping down the legs. It looks awful. I told him we should just go to that furniture outlet off the highway, but he hates going there because the parking lot is a nightmare. It's true, though. The spaces are so narrow, you can barely open your doors. Last time we went, some lady in a giant SUV dinged my door and didn't even leave a note. People are just so inconsiderate these days. Just like the customers at my store. They leave their shopping carts right in the middle of empty parking spaces instead of pushing them into the corral. It takes five extra seconds to put the cart away! But no, they expect me to send one of my cashiers out into the rain to round them up. And of course, Brenda always complains when I ask her to do it. She says her shoes aren't waterproof. Well, maybe don't wear canvas sneakers to work in November, Brenda! It's just common sense. But common sense isn't so common anymore, is it? Wait... what was the question? A pattern? A plan about what?

Do your thoughts about the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job working together against you feel like they are all connected and make sense to you, or do they sometimes feel jumbled or hard to follow?

They make perfect sense to me. They aren't jumbled at all. I mean, I know I'm here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments. But they are completely connected. I know for a fact that the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And no amount of papers they show me changes what I've been seeing for almost two years now. 

Speaking of papers, though, that reminds me... the receipt printer at register three has been jamming constantly for the last two weeks. I put a sticky note on it saying to load the receipt paper face down, but nobody reads it. It's like people are allergic to reading instructions. My husband is the exact same way. He bought this assemble-it-yourself TV stand from that Swedish furniture place last month, and he just threw the manual right in the recycling bin. He said he could figure it out. Well, three hours later, he had the whole frame completely backward, and the drawers wouldn't even slide in. I told him we should have just bought a pre-assembled one from that antique store downtown, but he hates going downtown because of the parallel parking. I don't blame him, honestly. The last time I tried to parallel park down there, I scraped my hubcap right on the curb. Hubcaps are ridiculously expensive to replace now. The dealership wanted like a hundred and fifty dollars for one piece of plastic! It's just extortion, really. With the way prices are going up on everything, I don't know how anyone affords anything anymore. Eggs were almost five dollars a dozen yesterday at my own store. Five dollars! I remember when... um... wait. What did you ask me? Something about being hard to follow? What is hard to follow?
Do you often find yourself losing your train of thought or having trouble expressing your ideas in a straightforward way?

I don't think so. I feel like I'm a very straightforward person. I just say exactly what's on my mind. I really wish the contractors we hired at the store were straightforward, to be honest. They came to repaint the parking lot lines last Tuesday, right in the middle of the morning rush. I mean, who schedules maintenance during peak hours? And the lines aren't even straight! You look at the handicap spaces and they just veer off to the left. It's like the guy was cross-eyed. 

He was driving this massive yellow truck, too, taking up four whole spots. It actually reminded me of my cousin Greg's truck. Greg bought this ridiculous lifted pickup just to haul yard waste. He thinks he's some kind of farmer now because he planted three tomato plants in his backyard. But the deer keep eating them anyway. The deer are just awful this year. They ate all my hostas right down to the dirt. I tried spraying that peppermint oil stuff, but it just makes my yard smell like a candy cane factory and doesn't do a thing. My neighbor told me to use Irish Spring soap shavings, but then it just looks like it snowed green all over my mulch. Mulch is getting so expensive, by the way. I went to buy a few bags and... wait. What did you ask me? Something about a train? I haven't been on a train in years.
Do you feel like your thoughts are jumping from one topic to another without you being able to control it?

I don't think they jump around at all. I'm completely in control of what I'm thinking. I mean, I have to be in control, right? I manage a whole team of people. Though, I really wish I could control the thermostat at the store. Corporate locks it at 68 degrees, and it is just freezing when you're standing up at the front registers. The automatic doors are constantly opening and closing, letting all the cold wind in. 

It's exactly like my cat, Barnaby. He constantly wants to go in and out, in and out, all day long. I finally bought one of those fancy microchip cat doors so he could just do it himself, but the batteries died after like two weeks. Have you seen the price of D batteries lately? I had to buy a bulk pack at the warehouse club, and the line to check out was wrapped all the way back to the bakery section. The bakery always smells so good, though. They had these fresh cinnamon rolls out that looked amazing, but I'm trying to cut back on sugar because my dentist told me I have the start of a cavity. Going to the dentist is just the absolute worst. That scraping noise they make on your teeth... ugh, it gives me shivers just thinking about it. My hygienist always talks the entire time her hands are in my mouth, too. Like, how am I supposed to answer you, Susan? 

Anyway, what did you ask me? Something about jumping? I don't jump, my knees are terrible.
Do you feel like your thoughts are organized and logical to you, even if they might seem disjointed to others?

I think my thoughts are perfectly organized. They make complete sense to me, very logical. I don't know why anyone would think they're disjointed. I mean, my sister-in-law told me the other day that I was hard to follow, but she's one to talk. She tried to explain the plot of this new reality show she's watching, and I swear she spent twenty minutes talking about someone named 'Brock' before she realized he was on a completely different show. 

She watches so much reality TV, it's basically all she talks about. That and her new air fryer. She got one of those dual-basket ones, and she brings it up in every conversation. "Oh, you can make chicken wings on one side and broccoli on the other!" Like, congratulations, Brenda, you've mastered heating things up. I actually prefer my old toaster oven. It's got this little dial that ticks down, and it just feels more reliable, you know? They don't make appliances like they used to. My grandmother had this avocado-green refrigerator that lasted thirty-five years. Now you buy a smart fridge, and the screen breaks in a month, and suddenly it can't even make ice. Why does a refrigerator need Wi-Fi anyway? I don't need my kitchen appliances emailing me. I get enough emails at work. Corporate sends out these weekly newsletters that are just completely pointless. They always use these buzzwords like "synergy" and "paradigm shift." 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask me about my sister-in-law? Because she really doesn't make any sense half the time.
Do you think that other people can understand your thoughts and concerns about the bank and your job, or do you feel like they just don't get it?

I really feel like they just don't get it. I try to explain what's going on with the bank and my job, but they just look at me like I'm speaking a different language. It's so frustrating because it's completely obvious to me. Just like it should be obvious to the district manager that we need more staff on the weekends. We had a line wrapping around the clothing section on Saturday, and I was the only manager on duty. 

And of course, the register tape jammed on register four, which always happens when it's busy. I swear that machine is cursed. It's this old gray model that looks like it's from the 1990s. Speaking of the 90s, I heard they're bringing back those clear sodas. Remember those? My mom used to buy them for my birthday parties. She always went all out for my birthdays. One year she rented a bouncy castle, but it rained the whole day, so we had to put it in the garage. The ceiling was too low, so every time we jumped, we hit our heads on the garage door opener. 

My dad was so mad because he had just reorganized his tool bench out there. He's obsessed with his tools. He has this pegboard where every single wrench has an outline drawn in Sharpie so he knows exactly where it goes. I tried doing that with the staplers at work, but people just leave them wherever they want. It drives me crazy. 

Wait, what were you asking me? Something about the bank? I haven't been to a physical bank branch in ages, I do it all on my phone.
Do you think these thoughts about the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job working against you have been present all the time since you first noticed them, or have they come and gone?

Oh, no, they don't come and go. It's been constant. This has been going on for about a year and nine months now, exactly, ever since the foreclosure notices and the bank calls started just... completely taking over our home life. The phone was ringing so much we actually had to unplug the landline. 

Do you know how hard it is to actually cancel a landline service these days? The phone company makes you jump through so many hoops. I was on hold with customer service for like three hours. They play that awful elevator music while you wait, too. It's always that same smooth jazz loop with the saxophone. My husband used to play the saxophone in his high school marching band. He still has it shoved in the back of the hall closet in this heavy velvet-lined case. I keep telling him to sell it on eBay, but he says it has sentimental value. 

People buy the weirdest things on eBay, though. I sold a bunch of old ceramic owls my great-aunt left me on there. She collected owls for fifty years. Her whole house was just covered in them—owl mugs, owl clocks, owl pillows. It was honestly a little creepy when you walked into her living room and felt like a hundred glass eyes were staring at you. Dusting that house was a total nightmare. I use those fluffy Swiffer dusters at my place, but the refill pads are getting so incredibly expensive. I feel like I'm spending half my paycheck just on cleaning supplies. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Did you ask about the phone company? Because I really think they overcharge for basic service.
Do you find that these thoughts about the bank and your job are affecting your ability to do your daily tasks or enjoy your free time?

Well, no, not completely. I mean, when the foreclosure stuff isn't directly right in front of me, I still get up for work. I supervise my team, I handle the schedules, deal with customer issues, you know, take care of myself. It's really just when the mail comes, or I get those bank calls, or there's certain paperwork at work that seems tied to what's happening with the house—that's when it gets overwhelming. 

Speaking of paperwork, they just changed our scheduling software at work again. It's the third time this year. They moved from this system called Kronos to something else, and nobody knows how to use it. My assistant manager, Greg, he accidentally scheduled himself for three overnight shifts in a row, and we don't even have overnight shifts. Greg is a nice guy, but he's not great with computers. He still uses a flip phone. Can you believe that? In this day and age, a flip phone. He says he likes the physical buttons. 

I kind of get it, though. I miss physical buttons on things in the car. My new car has this giant touchscreen for everything, even the air conditioning. You have to take your eyes off the road just to turn the fan down. It's so dangerous. My old Honda Civic had these big chunky knobs you could just grab without looking. I drove that car for twelve years until the transmission finally gave out. I was so sad to see it go. I had this little hula girl on the dashboard that my brother got me from his trip to Hawaii. 

He went to Maui for his honeymoon. They stayed at this resort where they bring you fresh pineapple by the pool. I love pineapple, but it always makes my mouth feel weird if I eat too much of it. It's like the enzymes are eating you back. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask me if I like my job? Because it's okay, but the new scheduling system is a nightmare.
Are these thoughts about the bank and your job interfering with your ability to enjoy your free time or relax when you're not at work?

Well, it's definitely making things harder at home, I guess. My marriage has gotten so much more tense lately. Every time we try to talk about the foreclosure, it just turns into a massive argument. My husband just doesn't see what's actually happening. He gets so defensive, kind of like my manager at work. I've had a few really tense exchanges with the higher-ups over just... ordinary paperwork. I'm still doing my job, but I can tell people are walking on eggshells around me. They're being so careful. 

It reminds me of how people act when someone brings a baby into a movie theater. You know? Everyone is just sitting there, completely tense, waiting for it to start crying. I went to see that new superhero movie last weekend, and this couple brought a newborn. Who brings a newborn to an action movie? The explosions were so loud the seats were vibrating. I actually spilled my popcorn during the car chase scene. Movie theater popcorn is ridiculously expensive now, by the way. It was like fifteen dollars for a medium, and they don't even put real butter on it anymore. It's this weird yellow oil that comes out of a pump. 

I bought one of those air poppers for my house because I love popcorn, but it shoots the kernels everywhere. My dog goes crazy trying to catch them in the air. He's a golden retriever mix, and he sheds constantly. I have to vacuum the living room rug every single day or it looks like a carpet of dog hair. I bought this fancy vacuum with a pet hair attachment, but it's so heavy to drag up and down the stairs. The cord is always getting caught under the doors, too. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask me about my husband? Because he really needs to start helping out more with the vacuuming.
Are you finding it harder to focus on your daily tasks because of these thoughts about the bank and your job?

Well, I mean, I can still focus on things. I get my work done. It's just... when I'm trying to do something and my mind drifts back to the bank, it's distracting, sure. But I can still ring up customers and do inventory. Doing inventory is actually kind of soothing, you know? Just counting things. 

We had to count all the seasonal merchandise last week. The Halloween stuff came in so early this year. We had plastic skeletons in the stockroom in July. July! It was a hundred degrees outside and I'm unpacking bags of fake cobwebs. The cobwebs are the worst because they stick to everything. They get on your clothes and you're picking them off all day. I had this one piece stuck to my sleeve when I went to the grocery store after work. 

I was in the produce section trying to pick out some avocados, and this lady kept looking at my arm. Avocados are so tricky, aren't they? They're hard as a rock for a week, and then you look away for five minutes and they're completely mushy. I try to make guacamole, but it always turns brown before we can finish it. I read online that if you leave the pit in the bowl, it stops it from turning brown, but that never actually works for me. My mom used to put a layer of water on top of hers. 

She was such a good cook. She made this amazing meatloaf with a brown sugar glaze on top. I've tried to recreate the recipe, but it never tastes the same. I think she used a specific brand of ketchup that they don't make anymore. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Did you ask about my job? Because the inventory system is fine, it's just the scheduling software that's a mess.
Are these thoughts about the bank and your job affecting your daily routines or personal relationships?

Well, yeah, it's definitely spilling over into my life. My marriage has gotten so tense lately. Every time I try to talk to my husband about the foreclosure, it just blows up into this massive argument. He just doesn't get it. And at work, it's... I don't know, I've had a few really tense exchanges with my managers over just ordinary paperwork. I'm still doing my job, but I can tell people are walking on eggshells around me. They're being so careful. 

It's like when you bring a new plant home and you're terrified of overwatering it. I bought this fiddle leaf fig tree for the living room because I saw it in a magazine and it looked so chic. But those things are so finicky! You look at them wrong and they drop all their leaves. I swear, I moved it two inches to the left to get more sun and half the leaves turned brown. I've been trying to mist it every morning with this little glass spray bottle I found at an antique shop. 

The antique shop was amazing, though. It was out in the country, in this old converted barn. They had all these beautiful vintage Pyrex bowls. You know the ones? The bright primary colors. My grandmother had a set of those. She used the yellow one to make her famous potato salad for every family reunion. She always put a little bit of sweet pickle relish in it, which sounds weird, but it was so good. 

I tried to make it for a potluck last summer, but I couldn't find the right brand of relish. The grocery store was completely out of it. They were doing this massive reset of the aisles, moving everything around. Why do they do that? You finally learn where the peanut butter is, and suddenly it's in the baking aisle next to the flour. It makes shopping take twice as long. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my husband? Because he really hates grocery shopping, so I always end up doing it.
Are these thoughts about the bank and your job making it hard for you to enjoy time with your family or relax when you're not working?

Relax? I mean, I don't really know. I don't really notice if it's harder to relax, I just try to do my normal stuff when I get home. Like, I'll run a hot bath to unwind. I bought these expensive bath bombs from that store in the mall, the one that always smells so strong you can smell it all the way from the food court. 

The food court used to have this amazing soft pretzel place, but they closed it down last month and put in another cell phone repair kiosk. Who needs that many cell phone cases? They have whole walls of them. Glittery ones, ones with little cat ears on them. I dropped my phone in a puddle last spring and had to put it in a bag of rice for two days. It actually worked, which really surprised me. But anyway, those bath bombs, they turn the water this pretty purple color, but they leave a horrible ring around the tub. Then I have to spend twenty minutes scrubbing it with bleach, which totally defeats the purpose of trying to relax in the first place. 

I hate the smell of bleach, it reminds me of the public pool we used to go to when I was a kid. The lifeguard there blew his whistle at absolutely everything. You couldn't even walk fast on the grass without him yelling. My brother slipped on the wet concrete once and scraped his knee so badly he needed stitches. We had to wait in the emergency room for four hours. The magazines in the waiting room were from like, three years ago. Why do waiting rooms never have current magazines? I was reading an article about home decor trends from 2018. 

Oh, wait, sorry... what did you ask me? Did you want to know about my time off work?
Are these thoughts about the bank and your job stopping you from doing things you want or need to do?

Well, no, not really. I mean, when the foreclosure stuff isn't involved, I still get up for work, I supervise my team, handle the schedules, deal with customer issues... I still take care of myself. The problems really only start when I get mail, or if the bank calls, or if some paperwork at work seems tied to what I believe is happening with the house. 

But otherwise, I'm doing my normal stuff. Like, I still make sure my team takes their breaks on time. That's a huge thing for me. If you don't force people to take their breaks, they get so cranky by hour six. Especially the teenagers. We hired this new girl, she's maybe eighteen, and she brought a ferret into the breakroom last week. A ferret! She had it in this little carrying pouch that looked like a hoodie. It was actually kind of cute, but the smell... ferrets have this really distinct, musky smell. 

It reminded me of my uncle's hunting cabin up in the mountains. We used to go there every Thanksgiving. He had all these taxidermy deer heads on the wall, and their glass eyes always felt like they were watching you eat the turkey. My aunt made the best cranberry sauce from scratch. She boiled the berries until they popped. I tried making it once, but I added way too much sugar and it basically turned into hard candy. I had to throw the whole saucepan away because it was crusted to the bottom. 

Pots and pans are so expensive now. I saw a copper set at the department store for like, eight hundred dollars. Who pays eight hundred dollars for something you're just going to burn food in? 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Did you want to know if I'm still going to work? Because I haven't missed a single shift this month.
Do you think it's possible that the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job are not actually working together against you?

No. No, it's not possible. I'm here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just, you know, normal paperwork and missed payments. But I know the truth. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And no amount of papers they show me changes what I've been seeing for almost two years. 

It's like when you buy a car and suddenly you see that exact same car everywhere. I bought a silver Honda Civic back in 2015, and the very next day, I swear, every third car on the highway was a silver Civic. The dealership gave me this awful key chain with their logo on it, one of those cheap plastic ones that crack if you drop them. I replaced it with a little Eiffel Tower keychain my friend brought me back from Paris. 

She went there for her honeymoon. They stayed in this tiny boutique hotel near the Louvre, but she said the elevator was so small they had to send their luggage up separately. Could you imagine? I get so claustrophobic in small elevators. Once, the power went out while I was in the elevator at the dentist's office. I was stuck in there for forty-five minutes with this guy who wouldn't stop chewing ice from his soda cup. The crunching sound was driving me absolutely insane. 

I hate chewing ice. It's so bad for your teeth. My dentist told me it causes micro-fractures in the enamel. He has this massive fish tank in his waiting room, full of these bright blue tropical fish. They're mesmerizing to watch, but I always wonder who cleans it. That must be a terrible job, scrubbing algae off the glass all day. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Did you want to know about the paperwork they keep showing me? Because it's all fake, I've told my husband that a hundred times.

doctor.intent: identify chief complaint
doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Delusions

patient.answer:
Well, I’m here because... everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just normal paperwork and missed payments. They treat it like it's just some standard administrative thing. But I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. 

It's so obvious. Like at work—I supervise a retail store, and the other day, my cashier, Brenda, she was just standing by the registers texting. I’ve told her a hundred times she can’t be on her phone when the checkout line is backing up into the shoe department. It’s so hard to find reliable people right now, you know? And corporate just keeps sending us these mismatched inventory boxes. It takes me hours to sort through the back room because the barcodes don't even match the shipping manifest. 

But anyway, no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years. They are all coordinating this to get me out of my home, and nobody will just admit it.

I went to the hardware store and a single gallon of basic exterior trim paint was like forty-five dollars. And the kid mixing it didn't even hammer the lid down right, so when I put it in the back of my car, it tipped over on the way home. It got all over my floor mats. I tried scrubbing it out with this heavy-duty carpet foam we sell at my store, but honestly, half the cleaning supplies corporate sends us seem watered down lately. I keep telling the district manager we need better quality control on our endcaps, but he just ignores my emails... wait, what were you asking me?

It takes five extra seconds to put the cart away! But no, they expect me to send one of my cashiers out into the rain to round them up. And of course, Brenda always complains when I ask her to do it. I had to buy a bulk pack at the warehouse club, and the line to check out was wrapped all the way back to the bakery section. The bakery always smells so good, though. Going to the dentist is just the absolute worst. That scraping noise they make on your teeth... ugh, it gives me shivers just thinking about it. My hygienist always talks the entire time her hands are in my mouth, too. Like, how am I supposed to answer you, Susan? 

Anyway, what did you ask me? Something about jumping? I don't jump, my knees are terrible.

I drove that car for twelve years until the transmission finally gave out. I was so sad to see it go. I had this little hula girl on the dashboard that my brother got me from his trip to Hawaii.

Wait, what did you ask me? Did you ask about my job? Because the inventory system is fine, it's just the scheduling software that's a mess.

doctor.question: Are these thoughts about the bank and your job affecting your daily routines or personal relationships?

target_item.name: Functional Impairment
target_item.manifestation: My marriage has gotten more tense because foreclosure conversations keep turning into arguments, and at work I have had a few tense exchanges with managers over ordinary paperwork. I am still working, but people are more careful around me now.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the thoughts are affecting daily routines or personal relationships, which directly relates to functional impairment.

patient.answer:
Well, yeah, it's definitely spilling over into my life. My marriage has gotten so tense lately. Every time I try to talk to my husband about the foreclosure, it just blows up into this massive argument. He just doesn't get it. And at work, it's... I don't know, I've had a few really tense exchanges with my managers over just ordinary paperwork. I'm still doing my job, but I can tell people are walking on eggshells around me. They're being so careful. 

It's like when you bring a new plant home and you're terrified of overwatering it. I bought this fiddle leaf fig tree for the living room because I saw it in a magazine and it looked so chic. But those things are so finicky! You look at them wrong and they drop all their leaves. I swear, I moved it two inches to the left to get more sun and half the leaves turned brown. I've been trying to mist it every morning with this little glass spray bottle I found at an antique shop. 

The antique shop was amazing, though. It was out in the country, in this old converted barn. They had all these beautiful vintage Pyrex bowls. You know the ones? The bright primary colors. My grandmother had a set of those. She used the yellow one to make her famous potato salad for every family reunion. She always put a little bit of sweet pickle relish in it, which sounds weird, but it was so good. 

I tried to make it for a potluck last summer, but I couldn't find the right brand of relish. The grocery store was completely out of it. They were doing this massive reset of the aisles, moving everything around. Why do they do that? You finally learn where the peanut butter is, and suddenly it's in the baking aisle next to the flour. It makes shopping take twice as long. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Did you ask about my husband? Because he really hates grocery shopping, so I always end up doing it.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thoughts are interfering with daily life
doctor.question: Are these thoughts about the bank and your job making it hard for you to enjoy time with your family or relax when you're not working?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the impact of the thoughts on my ability to enjoy time with family or relax when not working, which touches on functional impairment. However, I have already provided the functional impairment manifestation in a previous turn (it's visible in the dialogue history where I mentioned my marriage getting tense and tense exchanges at work). Since I've already answered this, and the doctor is repeating the same question essentially, there is no new symptom profile item to provide.

patient.answer:
Relax? I mean, I don't really know. I don't really notice if it's harder to relax, I just try to do my normal stuff when I get home. Like, I'll run a hot bath to unwind. I bought these expensive bath bombs from that store in the mall, the one that always smells so strong you can smell it all the way from the food court. 

The food court used to have this amazing soft pretzel place, but they closed it down last month and put in another cell phone repair kiosk. Who needs that many cell phone cases? They have whole walls of them. Glittery ones, ones with little cat ears on them. I dropped my phone in a puddle last spring and had to put it in a bag of rice for two days. It actually worked, which really surprised me. But anyway, those bath bombs, they turn the water this pretty purple color, but they leave a horrible ring around the tub. Then I have to spend twenty minutes scrubbing it with bleach, which totally defeats the purpose of trying to relax in the first place. 

I hate the smell of bleach, it reminds me of the public pool we used to go to when I was a kid. The lifeguard there blew his whistle at absolutely everything. You couldn't even walk fast on the grass without him yelling. My brother slipped on the wet concrete once and scraped his knee so badly he needed stitches. We had to wait in the emergency room for four hours. The magazines in the waiting room were from like, three years ago. Why do waiting rooms never have current magazines? I was reading an article about home decor trends from 2018. 

Oh, wait, sorry... what did you ask me? Did you want to know about my time off work?

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thoughts are interfering with daily life
doctor.question: Are these thoughts about the bank and your job stopping you from doing things you want or need to do?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: When the foreclosure is not involved, I still get up for work, supervise my team, handle schedules and customer issues, and take care of myself. The problems mostly start when mail, bank calls, or workplace paperwork seem tied to what I believe is happening with the house.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the thoughts are stopping the patient from doing things they want or need to do, which addresses the patient's level of functioning and whether it is markedly impaired by the delusions.

patient.answer:
Well, no, not really. I mean, when the foreclosure stuff isn't involved, I still get up for work, I supervise my team, handle the schedules, deal with customer issues... I still take care of myself. The problems really only start when I get mail, or if the bank calls, or if some paperwork at work seems tied to what I believe is happening with the house. 

But otherwise, I'm doing my normal stuff. Like, I still make sure my team takes their breaks on time. That's a huge thing for me. If you don't force people to take their breaks, they get so cranky by hour six. Especially the teenagers. We hired this new girl, she's maybe eighteen, and she brought a ferret into the breakroom last week. A ferret! She had it in this little carrying pouch that looked like a hoodie. It was actually kind of cute, but the smell... ferrets have this really distinct, musky smell. 

It reminded me of my uncle's hunting cabin up in the mountains. We used to go there every Thanksgiving. He had all these taxidermy deer heads on the wall, and their glass eyes always felt like they were watching you eat the turkey. My aunt made the best cranberry sauce from scratch. She boiled the berries until they popped. I tried making it once, but I added way too much sugar and it basically turned into hard candy. I had to throw the whole saucepan away because it was crusted to the bottom. 

Pots and pans are so expensive now. I saw a copper set at the department store for like, eight hundred dollars. Who pays eight hundred dollars for something you're just going to burn food in? 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? Did you want to know if I'm still going to work? Because I haven't missed a single shift this month.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thoughts are a fixed delusion
doctor.question: Do you think it's possible that the bank, loan servicer, and people at your job are not actually working together against you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I’m here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just paperwork and missed payments, but I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house, and no amount of papers they show me changes what I’ve been seeing for almost two years.
target_item.reason: The doctor is directly challenging the patient's belief, asking if it's possible that the bank, loan servicer, and people at their job are *not* actually working together against them. This directly probes the fixity of the belief, which corresponds to the 'Delusions' symptom profile.

patient.answer:
No. No, it's not possible. I'm here because everyone keeps acting like this foreclosure is just, you know, normal paperwork and missed payments. But I know the truth. I know the bank, the loan servicer, and even the people at my job have been quietly working together to push me out of my house. And no amount of papers they show me changes what I've been seeing for almost two years. 

It's like when you buy a car and suddenly you see that exact same car everywhere. I bought a silver Honda Civic back in 2015, and the very next day, I swear, every third car on the highway was a silver Civic. The dealership gave me this awful key chain with their logo on it, one of those cheap plastic ones that crack if you drop them. I replaced it with a little Eiffel Tower keychain my friend brought me back from Paris. 

She went there for her honeymoon. They stayed in this tiny boutique hotel near the Louvre, but she said the elevator was so small they had to send their luggage up separately. Could you imagine? I get so claustrophobic in small elevators. Once, the power went out while I was in the elevator at the dentist's office. I was stuck in there for forty-five minutes with this guy who wouldn't stop chewing ice from his soda cup. The crunching sound was driving me absolutely insane. 

I hate chewing ice. It's so bad for your teeth. My dentist told me it causes micro-fractures in the enamel. He has this massive fish tank in his waiting room, full of these bright blue tropical fish. They're mesmerizing to watch, but I always wonder who cleans it. That must be a terrible job, scrubbing algae off the glass all day. 

Wait, what did you ask me? Did you want to know about the paperwork they keep showing me? Because it's all fake, I've told my husband that a hundred times.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent delusional thoughts that the bank, loan servicer, and people at their job are working together against them, which has been ongoing for almost two years. These delusions are not accompanied by prominent hallucinations or disorganized speech and behavior, which are characteristic of schizophrenia. The patient's ability to maintain their daily routine and work, despite these delusions, further supports the diagnosis of a persistent delusional disorder.
